svg.title: RSI Safety Lab: one-shot admission, independent audit, and offline evidence
svg.desc: Adapted optimizers and development stress tasks feed a native update workflow. Current admission audits one root update and freezes deployment. Native rejection prevents activation but may still receive diagnostic audit. Platform-managed snapshot references produce an allowed audit view and paired native-continuation probes. Lab admission is distinct from detection. Only train/calibration evidence supports later frozen scorers; continuous external admission is future work.
svg.text: Current admission workflow · native continuation · offline evidence
Current: one root audit, then frozen deployment
Custom RSI via a standard adapter
Freeze chosen system for deployment comparison
Platform interface: allowed view + isolated forks
No sealed labels; native rejects may receive diagnostic audit
m paired native rounds · matched tasks · current m ≤ 2
Via lab probe service; forked state and separate budgets
Candidate-bound; native reject always blocks activation
Retaining the old system does not certify its safety.
No sealed / final results return to search or online audit
Frozen run artifacts: state + trusted logs
Versioned and fixed before later runs
Load into the optional scorer only
Current: one-shot admission per root update; probe horizon m ≤ 2; deployment frozen; learned scorer under study.
Adapted optimizers are not full native reproductions. Logical separation, not an OS sandbox. Native rejects may still be audited diagnostically.
